extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons users: institutional signing officials, account administrators, PIs, reviewers, research administrators, and other organization personnel who manage NIH grant accounts
extracted.subtask_short: eRA Commons user roles and passwords
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for eRA Commons user roles, their privileges, account/affiliation management, and eRA account password policies and procedures for NIH grantee organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account Administrator (AA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated by the SO, the AA facilitates the administration of eRA Commons accounts for their own organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you hold an AA role, you have privileges to: Create accounts and modify all Commons roles except IAR and FCOI roles; Reset passwords for users at their organization; Create affiliation between an existing PI or IAR Commons account and the organization. The AA typically is located in the Central Research Administration Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Official (AO)
rubrics_metrics.description: An AO is an official within an extramural organization who may be located within Central Research Administration and/or an academic department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you hold an AO role, you have privileges to: Create all accounts other than IAR, TRAINEE, and FCOI; Update Commons accounts created by the AO; View status and award information for all organization grants; Create affiliation between an existing PD/PI or IAR Commons account and the organization. NOTE: The AO cannot view summary statements or priority scores. NOTE: An AO is not authorized to submit reports to the NIH. SO and AO authorities should not be combined; if the same person is both, only SO authority is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant (ASST)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ASST user can perform tasks on behalf of a PD/PI depending on the authority granted to the ASST user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you hold an ASST role, you may have privileges to: Edit your own personal profile (PPF) data; Edit the PD/PI's PPF if delegated by a PI user; Edit the PD/PI's progress report data if delegated; View the PD/PI Grant Status if delegated; Perform PD/PI xTrain functions (except submit to agency) if delegated. Authority depends on delegation by the PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business Official (BO)
rubrics_metrics.description: A BO has signature or other authority related to administering grantee organization training grants and works in the xTrain module and IBO Portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you hold a BO role, you can: View Trainee Roster, List of Grants, Grant Summary, Routing History, PDF-formatted Appointments/Amendments/Terminations; Initiate, update, route, and submit Termination Notices (if authorized); Certify Loan Repayment Program (LRP) applicants using the IBO Portal. Agency-specific note: DOC does not use this role for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: FCOI users manage the Financial Conflict of Interest reporting process; the FCOI role can only be assigned by the SO to someone within their organization who has a Commons account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you hold an FCOI role, you have privileges to: Initiate FCOI; View and Edit FCOI; Delete FCOI; Submit FCOI. FCOI responsibilities can be shared by assigning FCOI_ASST or FCOI_View roles. Agency-specific: DOC does not use this role for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI Assistant (FCOI_ASST)
rubrics_metrics.description: FCOI_ASST users assist in working on the FCOI reporting process and are assigned by the SO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCOI_ASST privileges: Initiate FCOI; Search FCOI; View FCOI; Edit FCOI; Delete FCOI. NOTE: Assign FCOI_View to users who only need read-only access; assign FCOI_ASST for users who need to perform data entry and edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI Read-Only (FCOI_View)
rubrics_metrics.description: FCOI_View role grants authority to search for and view FCOI information entered by the organization in the FCOI module but not to perform data entry or changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCOI_View privileges: Search FCOI; View FCOI. NOTE: Assign FCOI_ASST instead for users needing to initiate, edit, or delete FCOI reports. Agency-specific: DOC does not use this role for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Report (FSR Role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FSR role is assigned for completing Federal Financial Report (FFR) responsibilities; the FFR is a statement of expenditures for a grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you hold an FSR role, you have privileges to submit FFRs on behalf of your organization. NOTE: An account with only the FSR role can only perform FSR tasks. Depending on workflow, SO or BO/AO may also have FSR responsibilities and these authorities may be combined on the same account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet Assisted Review (IAR)
rubrics_metrics.description: IAR users are Reviewers selected by Scientific Review Officers (SROs) to critique and score applications using the IAR module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IAR privileges: Edit your own personal profile (PPF) and Reviewer address data; Use IAR to submit critiques and preliminary scores for applications for meetings for which you are enabled. Many PD/PIs are enabled for IAR; other reviewers who have never served as PD/PIs have IAR authority only. If affiliated with an organization, IAR affiliation may allow other Commons features. Tip: Reviewers should consult the IAR for Reviewers online help system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Director/Principal Investigator (PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: A PI (displayed as PI) directs a research project or program supported by NIH and is required for certain submissions like LRP applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI privileges: Edit personal profile (PPF); Delegate edit authority of your PPF; View status of all grant applications for which you are designated PI, including errors/warnings; View assembled image of submitted grant applications; View Study Section/Meeting Roster of review group; View Review outcome information and summary statements; View Notice of Award (NoA) for grants where designated PI; Delegate authority to ASSTs to perform actions and receive notifications; Submit an LRP application. Additional xTrain privileges: view Trainee Roster, List of Grants, Grant Summary, Routing History, PDF-formatted Appointments/Amendments/Terminations; Initiate/update/route/submit Appointments, Re-Appointments, Amendments, Termination Notices; Initiate a progress report and delegate progress report authority; Submit a progress report when given authority by an SO; Delegate Status authority (except Review outcome info and Summary Statement). NOTES: PI users cannot delegate authority to submit appointments to the agency. PI role should not be combined with the SO role but can be combined with IAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing Official (SO)
rubrics_metrics.description: An SO has authority to legally bind the organization in award administration matters and provide signature approval on award application submissions; SOs are required for many institution-level activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO privileges: Create additional SO accounts (SO is the only role that can create SO accounts); Register the applicant organization in Commons; Create and update the Institutional Profile (IPF); Create/delete/update all Commons accounts (except IAR and TRAINEE); Create affiliation between PD/PI and/or IAR account and the organization; Submit award applications via Grants.gov if also registered as the AOR; View status of all applications originating from their organization including errors/warnings; View Review outcome information including summary statement, overall impact score and percentile; View assembled image of submitted award applications; Reject award applications to address submission warnings; View award information for all awards granted to the organization; Submit JIT information for a PD/PI; View xTrain items (Trainee Roster, List of Grants, Grant Summary, Routing History, PDFs); Delegate and submit progress reports; Submit Final RPPR; Submit a one-time No-Cost Extension; Assign the FCOI role for FCOI module. RECOMMENDATION: Maintain at least two SO accounts at all times because SO is crucial for many eRA activities; if only one SO exists and becomes unavailable, contact the eRA Service Desk. NOTE: The SO role cannot be combined with a PI role. Agency-specific instructions: not all agencies utilize delegation the same way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor (SPONSOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sponsor supervises the research training experience of individual fellows supported by fellowship awards in the xTrain module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor privileges: View Training Grant related items such as Trainee Roster and List of Grants; Review Termination Notices and route to BO before submission to Agency; Initiate Termination Notices on behalf of fellows who have left the organization; Delegate Sponsor authority to another individual. Agency-specific: DOC does not use this role for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee (TRAINEE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The TRAINEE role manages electronic appointments for awarded Training Grants in the xTrain module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRAINEE privileges: View PDF-formatted Appointments/Amendments/Terminations; Update and route Appointments/Amendments/Terminations; View routing history. Agency-specific: DOC does not use this role for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoc / Graduate / Undergraduate / Project Personnel roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Roles assigned to individuals based on their participation level on NIH-funded projects (POSTDOC, Graduate, Undergraduate, Project Personnel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POSTDOC: Role exists for those serving in a postdoctoral role (mentored, not necessarily permanent). Graduate/Undergraduate: Assigned to individuals participating in an NIH-funded project for at least one person month; see NOT-OD-13-097 for details. Project Personnel: Assigned to individuals performing other project roles. Guidance: refer to the referenced guide notice (NOT-OD-13-097) for more information. Agency-specific: some roles may not give privileges for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access Compliance Report (PACR)
rubrics_metrics.description: PACR role provides access to the Public Access Compliance Report system via the Commons home page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having this role provides access to PACR; no additional privilege list provided in this chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Switching Institutions — keep single Commons account
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for PIs who move between organizations: maintain a single Commons account and affiliate with the new organization rather than creating a new account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits: grant record history remains together; reviewer service recorded for continuous submission eligibility; records more accurate; degree information retained for Early Stage Investigator eligibility. Steps: 1) Request SO at new organization affiliate your existing account (provide Commons ID). 2) If you left the old organization, request SO there disaffiliate you. NOTE: One Commons account can have multiple affiliations; you don't need to disaffiliate from the first organization if you still remain there. 3) Contact eRA Service Desk if you have more than one Commons account to merge. 4) Keep your Commons Personal Profile updated (address fields and employment end dates). IMPORTANT: While a PI can keep the same Commons account when switching institutions, system users with the SO role must create a new account within the new organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing to a Different Affiliated Organization (session selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: If affiliated with multiple organizations, you must select which organization to work with in a Commons session; you access only information and roles granted by the currently selected organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: 1) Log in to eRA Commons. 2) Click the Person icon; if affiliated with multiple organizations, click Change Organization. 3) Choose the organization from the list and click Save to set default. Your session will show grant data and roles associated with the selected organization. Note: selected organization is displayed under the Person icon and you possess only the roles granted by that organization for the session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening Modules & module visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To navigate between eRA Commons modules, use the Main menu/eRA logo or home-screen buttons; you only see modules/features that your user roles give you access to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you can't find a module, it's likely because your roles do not give access. User roles are assigned by your institutional SO, AO, or AA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logging out best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: For security reasons it is a best practice to log off from the Commons system upon completion of any work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To logout, click the Person icon at upper right of any screen and select Sign out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password Policy and Requirements for eRA account credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and lifecycle rules for eRA account passwords (users are transitioning to two-factor authentication methods but still must maintain an eRA account password and change it at least once per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Password requirements: Must be at least fifteen (15) characters long; Case sensitive; May contain spaces; Should not include your name, address, phone number, Social Security number, date of birth, HHS ID, etc.; Does not need to contain numbers, capital letters, or special characters; Cannot contain weak/overused terms such as "password."; Should not match current or past passwords from work or personal accounts; Cannot reuse the previous ten passwords; Must be changed once per year. Account lockout: Accounts locked after 5 consecutive failed login attempts within a 120-minute period; lockout lasts 30 minutes or until reset by an authorized administrator. Temporary passwords: sent via email and valid only for 48 hours. Users are prompted to change temporary passwords at first login.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-factor authentication note (Login.gov / InCommon)
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA users are being transitioned to require two-factor authentication using Login.gov or an InCommon Federated account, but continue to maintain an eRA account and password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when using Login.gov or InCommon Federated accounts for two-factor authentication, users must continue to change the eRA account password at least once per year. Links provided for Login.gov password management and FAQs; see eRA FAQs for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resetting Forgotten Passwords and account lockout recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for resetting an eRA account password when forgotten or when an account is locked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps to reset forgotten password: Click Forgot Password/Unlock Account? link, enter User ID and Email, Submit; Commons generates a temporary password sent to the email in the user profile (valid 48 hours); log in with temporary password and create a new password that meets the policy. If the account is locked from too many failed attempts, wait 15 minutes before reset by self or organization's SO/AA; if you don't have access to the email associated with your account, contact an SO or AA to reset password and change the email; if you cannot locate SO/AA, contact the eRA Service Desk. IMPORTANT: Don't use browser 'save password' option; clear cache if old password reappears in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing Your Password (normal/expired flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to change your eRA account password while logged in or when password expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change while logged in: Access Change Password screen via Admin module or Person icon; enter current password, new password and confirm (must meet Password Requirements) and Submit. For expired/reset password: Enter Current Password, Enter New Password, Confirm, Select Submit; new password is effective immediately. Passwords display as dots; avoid browser save password option. Note: eRA still prompts annual password change even if using two-factor authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting a New Signing Official Account (if no active SOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and prerequisites for the eRA Service Desk to create a new SO account when an organization has no active signing official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements before initiating request: Organization's SAM.gov registration must be active; the Electronic Business Point of Contact (eBiz POC) associated with SAM.gov registration must still be active at the organization and must contact the eRA Service Desk using their registered email address; the eBiz POC must have access to the email associated with the SAM.gov registration. The eBiz POC submits a request to the eRA Service Desk; the request is evaluated. If granted, Service Desk gathers information (name, preferred user ID, contact) and the new SO receives two emails: first with Commons ID, second with temporary password (valid 48 hours). The new SO should immediately log in, change password, and create another SO account for a second member of the organization. If the organization still has at least one active SO, this process does not apply; the remaining SO can create additional SO accounts using Create or Edit a Commons Account.
